title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting and notation. This is the last page of an English letter, signed 'Sincerely your's', commenting on someone's written notes of a talk by Grothendieck on the standard conjectures. X is smooth projective of dimension n. Y is a smooth hyperplane section with inclusion φ: Y→X. The basic identities are φ_*φ^* = L_X and φ^*φ_* = L_Y. 'Algebraic' means lying in the Q-span of cycle classes, or being induced by an algebraic correspondence. The subscript χ is presumably the coefficient field of the Weil cohomology.

The letter's notation is not the Bombay notation (1968).
- C(X) here is the Lefschetz-type conjecture: algebraic inverses to L^{n-i}, i.e. Λ is algebraic. The previous page gives it as 'existence of algebraic isomorphisms H^{2n-i}→H^i'. This is B(X) in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles'.
- A(X) is the weak form: L^{n-2i} induces an isomorphism on algebraic classes. If L^{n-2i}x is algebraic then x is algebraic. This is A(X,L) in Bombay.
- A(X)° denotes A restricted to the critical degree.

The page first closes the previous discussion. The semisimplicity of the correspondence ring, given C plus the Hodge index condition I(X×X), and the deduction of Weil from C and A, should go in an extra paragraph of 'the notes'.

The 'last and rather trivial remark' introduces two hyperplane-section conditions.
- A'(X): for 2i ≤ n-1, if x ∈ H^i(X) and φ^*x is algebraic, then x is algebraic. This is a weak-Lefschetz injectivity statement on cycles.
- A''(X): for 2i ≥ n-1, every algebraic class in H^{i+2}(X) is φ_* of an algebraic class of H^i(Y). This is a Gysin-surjectivity statement on cycles.
- A'°, A''° restrict these to the critical degrees: 2i = n-1 if n is odd, 2i = n-2 if n is even. The 'i' here seems to be a cycle codimension, not a cohomological degree; the indexing is loose.

Why these are 'weak'. A(X) implies A'. Indeed φ_*φ^*x = L_X x is algebraic, hence so is L^{n-2i}x, hence so is x. C(Y) is claimed to imply A'', via y = Λ_Y φ^*(x).

The Proposition. C(X) is equivalent to C(Y) + A'°(X×X) + A''°(X×X). By induction (Y, then Z a section of Y, and so on) C(X) is equivalent to A'° and A''° for X×X, Y×Y, Z×Z, .... There is an analogous statement with X×Y, Y×Z, and so on.

The underlying mechanism, not spelled out here but standard (Grothendieck/Kleiman), is this. The class of Λ_X lies in H^{2n-2}(X×X), which is exactly the critical degree of the 2n-dimensional X×X. Also L^2_{X×X}Λ is computably algebraic. So A°(X×X) gives C(X), and the converse is easy.

Key lemma. A(X)° follows from A'°, A''° (and the C of the hyperplane section), by factoring the Lefschetz operator through the hyperplane section.

Even case, dim X = 2m. Factor L^2 = L_X∘φ_*∘φ^*: H^{2m-2}(X)→H^{2m-2}(Y)→H^{2m}(X)→H^{2m+2}(X).
- Suppose L^2x is algebraic. A'' gives an algebraic y ∈ H^{2m}(Y) with φ_*y = L^2x.
- Since φ_*: H^{2m}(Y)→H^{2m+2}(X) is an isomorphism (2m > dim Y), y = L_Yφ^*x.
- C(Y) then gives φ^*x = Λ_Y y algebraic, and A' gives x algebraic.

Odd case, dim X = 2m+1. Factor L = φ_*φ^*: H^{2m}(X)→H^{2m}(Y)→H^{2m+2}(X).

Purpose. This reduces the Lefschetz standard conjecture, by induction on dimension, to two 'weak Lefschetz'-type statements about algebraic cycles under restriction to, and Gysin from, hyperplane sections, applied only in the critical degree of self-products.
errors: The recipe y = Λ_Y φ^*(x) for A'' cannot be right in general. One only gets L_X(φ_*y − x) = 0, or φ^*(φ_*y − x) = 0, and neither L_X nor φ^* is injective in the relevant degrees. Counterexample: X = P^n with x the point class in H^{2n}(X). Then φ^*x = 0, so φ_*Λ_Yφ^*x = 0 ≠ x, although A'' itself holds there. Outside the critical degree, C(Y) alone seems to give A''(X) only modulo inverting L_X, i.e. modulo an A(X)-type statement. So 'trivially implied by C(Y)' needs more argument, except perhaps exactly at the critical degree with a suitable normalisation of Λ_Y.

Odd-dimensional case of the key lemma: A'' gives an algebraic y ∈ H^{2m}(Y) (middle degree of Y) with φ_*y = Lx. But φ_* is not injective there; its kernel is the vanishing cohomology. Concluding that φ^*x is algebraic requires an algebraic projection of H^{2m}(Y) onto φ^*H^{2m}(X). That is a left-inverse problem of exactly the kind the previous page says needs Λ_X (i.e. C(X)) or semisimplicity. As written, the odd case has a gap.
The lemma silently uses C of the hyperplane section, not only A'° and A''°, although the Proposition does list C(Y).

In the Proposition, A'°/A''° are applied to X×X. Running the lemma there involves a hyperplane section W of X×X and needs C(W), whereas the Proposition lists C(Y) for Y a section of X. W is not Y×Y, and dim W grows rather than drops. The induction X×X, Y×Y, Z×Z, ... is therefore not justified as stated. Perhaps the reducible ample divisor Y×X + X×Y is intended, which would explain the 'analogous statement with X×Y, Y×Z'; this is not explained.
Index conventions are loose. 'Critical dimensions 2i = n-1 / n-2' treats i as a codimension, while A', A'' use i as a cohomological degree.

ideas.what: Reduce the Lefschetz-type conjecture C(X) (= B(X)) to the weak Lefschetz form A in the critical degree of X×X, using that the class of Λ_X lies in H^{2n-2}(X×X)
ideas.modern_name: B(X) ⇔ A(X×X) (Lefschetz standard conjecture vs. its weak form on X×X)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay Colloquium 1968); Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés)

ideas.what: Hyperplane-section 'weak Lefschetz for algebraic cycles' conditions A' (restriction to Y detects algebraicity below the middle) and A'' (Gysin from Y is surjective on algebraic classes above the middle)
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz hyperplane theorem for algebraic classes / cycle-theoretic weak Lefschetz
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (variants appear in later discussions of the standard conjectures, e.g. Kleiman's surveys)
ideas.where_published: Not in the Bombay text as far as I know

ideas.what: Factorisation L^2 = L∘φ_*∘φ^* (even dim) and L = φ_*φ^* (odd dim) to deduce the critical-degree A(X)° from A'°, A''° and C(Y); induction on dimension via hyperplane sections
ideas.modern_name: inductive reduction of the Lefschetz standard conjecture to hyperplane sections

ideas.what: Plan to explain semisimplicity of the correspondence ring from C + Hodge index on X×X, and the deduction of Weil from C and A
ideas.modern_name: semisimplicity of homological motives under the standard conjectures; Weil conjectures from standard conjectures
ideas.where_published: Bombay 1968 talk; Kleiman, Dix exposés 1968; Jannsen 1992 for semisimplicity of numerical motives

missed.claim: The Lefschetz standard conjecture is equivalent, by induction on dimension, to two weak-Lefschetz-type statements for algebraic cycles: injectivity of restriction to a hyperplane section on cycle classes (A'), and surjectivity of Gysin on algebraic classes (A''). These are needed only in the critical degree of self-products. The proof sketch has gaps (odd case; which hyperplane section of X×X), and as far as I know this exact formulation was not developed in print.
missed.quote: The remark then is that these pretendedly "week" variants in fact imply the full Lefschets relations for algebraic cycles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Recent approaches to the Lefschetz standard conjecture study algebraic classes on hyperplane sections and vanishing cohomology, e.g. Charles' remarks on the Lefschetz standard conjecture and hyperkähler varieties. A clean cycle-theoretic weak-Lefschetz criterion, once repaired (e.g. by adding an algebraic projection onto φ^*H(X) in the middle degree of Y), would be a usable reduction.

deep.surprise_reason: The core equivalence C(X) ⇔ A(X×X) is published (Bombay, Kleiman). The repackaging via hyperplane-section 'weak' conditions A', A'' and induction is a mildly notable unpublished variant. It is also sketchy: the odd case, the formula y = Λ_Yφ^*x, and the choice of hyperplane section of X×X all have gaps, so it is not a finished uncredited result.
transcription_corrections: 'Proposition B_χ(X) [?]': the letter appears to be a C typed over another letter (E/B); in context it should read C_χ(X), the Lefschetz-type condition.
'A_χ(X)°' in 'This comes from the remark that...' is typed as A_χ(X××)° with the extra characters struck out, so it reads A_χ(X)°.
A''_χ(X) as corrected by hand: 'if 2i ≥ n-1, any algebraic element of H^{i+2}(X) is the image of an algebraic element of H^i(Y)'. The '≥' is a handwritten correction.
In the odd case the source is typed 'H^{2m+1-1}(X) → H^{2m+1+1}(X)' with an overstrike; it means H^{2m}(X) → H^{2m+2}(X).
Handwritten 'x' inserted after 'element' in A'; 'pretendedly' corrected by hand; 'algebraic' corrected from 'albraic'.
